items.title: Youcef Belaïli au MC Alger : son salaire suscite la controverse
items.description: Youcef Belaili , est de retour en championnat Algérie, après deux saisons passées en Tunisie, avec l’ES Tunis. L’attaquant international algérien s'est engagé avec le MC Alger après plusieurs semaines de négociations et de rebondissements. Pour ce retour au Doyen où il a joué durant la saison 2023-2024, l’ancien joueur d’Ajaccio percevra avec un salaire mirobolant de 65.000 euros par mois soit près de 18 millions de dinars (1,8 milliards de centimes au taux de change parallèle), selon plusieurs médias spécialisés dont Compétition. Dans ce contexte, une interrogation demeure : comment le champion d’Algérie en titre compte-t-il rémunérer sa nouvelle recrue, alors que la FAF a plafonné les salaires des joueurs professionnels ? Le feuilleton du transfert de Belaïli de l’ES Tunis au MC Alger a pris fin le 24 juillet. Dans un communiqué publié le jour même, le club tunisien a annoncé avoir clos définitivement le dossier du renouvellement du contrat de son joueur. L’ES Tunis a expliqué qu'après « l'épuisement de toutes les phases de négociation et l'expiration de tous les délais convenus entre les différentes parties », il a été décidé de mettre un terme aux discussions avec son désormais ex-attaquant. L'Espérance a rappelé qu'un accord de principe avait été conclu le 5 juin entre les dirigeants du club et Youcef Belaïli. Celui-ci prévoyait une prolongation de deux saisons afin de préserver « les piliers de l'équipe et d'assurer sa stabilité sportive ». Le club affirme également avoir accompagné l'international algérien dans son litige avec la FIFA, notamment en mettant à sa disposition tous les documents nécessaires pour défendre son dossier devant le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS). En mars dernier, la FIFA a infligé une suspension d’une année à Belaili, dans le cadre du litige qui l’oppose à son ancien club, AC Ajaccio où il a évolué durant la saison 2022-2023 Après deux rendez-vous manqués pour effectuer la visite médicale et signer le contrat, l'ES Tunis a finalement décidé de mettre un terme aux négociations. « Tout en souhaitant à Mohamed Youcef Belaïli pleine réussite pour la suite de sa carrière, la direction assure que l'intérêt de l'Espérance Sportive de Tunis, le prestige du club, le respect de sa parole et de ses engagements demeurent toujours prioritaires », conclut le communiqué. Le MC Alger officialise un accord avec Youcef Belaili Quelques heures plus tard, peu avant minuit, le MC Alger a annoncé avoir trouvé un accord définitif avec Youcef Belaïli. Le club précise que le joueur retrouvera les Vert et Rouge pour la saison 2026-2027 et que « les deux parties se sont entendues sur l'ensemble des modalités financières ainsi que sur les différents autres aspects du contrat ». Toutefois, le Mouloudia précise que cet accord ne prendra officiellement effet qu'après la décision définitive du Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) concernant la sanction infligée au joueur par la FIFA et après une visite médicale concluante. Belaïli relance le débat sur le plafonnement des salaires des joueurs par la FAF Selon Compétition, Youcef Belaïli a négocié un salaire de 65.000 euros par mois pour un contrat de deux saisons avec le MC Alger. Cette information soulève toutefois des interrogations au regard des nouvelles règles instaurées par la Fédération algérienne de football (FAF). Depuis la saison 2025-2026, la FAF a adopté un nouveau contrat-type pour les joueurs professionnels. Celui-ci prévoit un salaire mensuel plafonné à 300 000 dinars, soit environ 2 000 euros au taux de change officiel. Les nouvelles dispositions prévoient également que les salaires et les primes de l'ensemble des joueurs, qu'ils soient algériens ou étrangers, soient versés en dinars algériens. En pratique, ce plafond concerne toutefois le salaire fixe. Les contrats peuvent également inclure une prime à la signature ainsi que des primes de performance, qui représentent une part importante de la rémunération globale. À ce stade, ni le MC Alger ni Youcef Belaïli n'ont communiqué les détails financiers du contrat. Les informations avancées par la presse spécialisée n'ont pas été confirmées officiellement. Si le montant de 65 000 euros mensuels venait à être confirmé, il relancerait le débat sur l'application des nouvelles règles salariales mises en place par la FAF et sur les mécanismes permettant aux clubs de rémunérer leurs joueurs vedettes. L’article Youcef Belaïli au MC Alger : son salaire suscite la controverse est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The Preacher
items.description: Read more about the Democrats who might run for president in 2028 here . G overnor Wes Moore doesn’t care about saving the Democratic Party; if anything, he thinks it has stood in his way. When we met up in May, he quoted Jay-Z: “ Industry shady, it need to be taken over .” The 2001 track is about Jay-Z’s rise to fame, and the ways the recording industry tried to exploit and co-opt him because he was “raisin’ the status quo up .” Moore was talking about a failed political system, and a Democratic Party that, he told me, “tried as hard as they could to get me not to run.” Jay-Z describes himself as a “renegade,” and Moore would like to be seen in a similar light—as the outsider who got himself to the top. Moore is the first Black governor of Maryland and the only Black governor serving in America today. At 47, he’s a relative newcomer to politics—he was the head of Robin Hood, a poverty-fighting foundation, until 2021—but he’s already being discussed as a possible presidential candidate in 2028. He’s just the kind of Bronze Star–winning, God-praising, son-of-an-immigrant Rhodes Scholar whom many Democratic voters would see as a dream candidate (although he denied to me that he was considering running). But so far, his tenure as governor has been far from smooth. In May 2025, he surprised many people by vetoing a bill establishing a commission to study the economic effects of slavery and racism on the state’s citizens and to recommend policies that could include reparations. Black legislators were outraged, and the Maryland General Assembly eventually overrode his veto. Moore defended his decision by dismissing the commission as a body conducting mere academic research, when what people needed was real change: “I am not a believer in studies, commissions,” he told me. “I’m like, Are we doing the work or not? ” He pointed to big investments in HBCUs and a mass pardon for cannabis convictions as proof of his progressive accomplishments. [ Richard D. Kahlenberg: The Democrats can’t let go of racial preferences ] Moore likes to portray himself as an independent actor, beholden to no one. He has signed legislation that prevents 16- and 17-year-olds from being tried as adults for some crimes, and also increased funding for the police. He has, he boasted to me, vetoed “more bills than any Democratic governor in the history of the state of Maryland” because he doesn’t believe in passing “unfunded mandates.” And he doesn’t care whether the party likes it or not: “I didn’t win because of the Democratic Party,” he said. “I won in spite of the Democratic Party.” He added: “I don’t come from nothing, and I didn’t need nothing, and I’m not owned by anybody. When I’m making my decisions, there is no party boss that I call.” Although this message seems tailor-made for this moment, in which so many Americans are simultaneously highly partisan yet disgusted by both parties, Moore’s approval rating in Maryland has fallen below 50 percent for the first time. (He’s still expected to win easily in the November election—he won 88 percent of the vote in the June primary, and one of his staffers shared with me an internal poll that found a higher approval rating.) He’s facing a number of challenges, particularly the dogged perception that he lacks authenticity—that he hasn’t been honest about who he really is. Moore has a politician’s powder-white smile and a bald head that shines like glass. I met him this spring, in Selma, Alabama, where he’d gone to commemorate the anniversary of Bloody Sunday, when about 600 civil-rights marchers were attacked on the Edmund Pettus Bridge. He began the weekend with a speech at Brown Chapel AME Church. “I know we are built for this, because I know what we are built of,” he told the mostly Black crowd. He listed heroes of the civil-rights movement and then said, “This is our time,” holding up his index finger like a Baptist preacher. Everywhere he went, lines formed. And he played his role perfectly. A bear hug for Governor J. B. Pritzker of Illinois. A selfie for a Black teenager with braces. “Good morning! Good morning! Good morning! How’s everybody doin’?” Then, pulling on the words like a southerner: “Alllll riiiiiight.” An hour or so later, at the Historic Tabernacle Baptist Church, his words tipped toward preaching: “I know where my worthiness comes from, and it does not come from Washington, D.C.” A few weeks later, on the Baltimore Orioles’ Opening Day, he stepped out of a black SUV wearing an orange jersey with his name on the back, and a man rushed up to him: “Sign my baseball for when you run for president.” “Not going to happen,” Moore quickly responded—while signing his name. Over the next few months, I watched Moore go from boat ride to baseball game to matcha tasting to college-graduation speech. In every situation, he knew exactly who to be. By the time he quoted Jay-Z to me, I understood that he had me pegged, too. Don Smallwood for The Atlantic Moore and his wife, Dawn, speaking to families at their official residence in June. I was fascinated by Moore’s ability to adapt to his different audiences. I grew up having to do the same, and although I appreciate that I can connect with people from both elite and underprivileged backgrounds, I wish I were as much of a natural as he is. Even as a journalist at The Atlantic , I still find myself sometimes intimidated, my voice trembling. Moore moved like water. But this may be one reason some voters struggle to trust him. When I asked people I know in Maryland, many of them Black, what they think of the governor, I heard things such as He doesn’t say what he means and We don’t know what his agenda is . They thought it was weird that he won without having any political experience. That distrust has been fueled by persistent negative reporting from conservative media outlets. At the Orioles game, a white man in a USA shirt said, “I appreciate you, Gov,” as Moore autographed his collection of baseball cards. Then Moore walked onto the field, and many people in the stadium booed. He smiled and clapped for himself, and seemed to take no notice of the crowd’s displeasure. About that Bronze Star. Moore has been accused of making what The Washington Free Beacon called “a litany of false statements about his family history, his upbringing, and his academic, athletic, and military achievements.” The accusations range from minor to significant, and begin with his hometown. The text on the back cover of his 2010 book, The Other Wes Moore: One Name, Two Fates , reads: “Two kids named Wes Moore were born blocks apart.” Both “grew up fatherless in similar Baltimore neighborhoods and had difficult childhoods.” In fact, Moore’s first years were spent in Takoma Park, Maryland—a nice suburb of Washington, which I know because I live about five minutes away. The book itself does mention that his family home was on “the border of Maryland and Washington, D.C.” But many people who read the book still come away with the impression that Moore was born and raised in Baltimore. It’s true that he grew up fatherless. Moore was 3 when his father died of a virus; he believes that a racist health-care system gave him shoddy treatment. His mother moved with Moore and his sisters to the Bronx, to be closer to her family. He attended the elite Riverdale Country School, but after his grades dropped and he got caught with a smoke bomb in the locker room as a prank, his mother sent him to Valley Forge Military Academy, in Pennsylvania. (His grandparents took out a second mortgage to help pay the tuition.) He moved back to Baltimore only as a college student, to go to Johns Hopkins University. He was living there in 2015 when the city erupted in protests following the death of Freddie Gray, who suffered a spinal-cord injury while inside a police van. Moore co-authored an account of that period with Erica L. Green, Five Days: The Fiery Reckoning of an American City . (“I am from Baltimore,” he wrote in that book.) He later kept a home in the city while commuting to Robin Hood in New York. After his Baltimore bonafides came under scrutiny in 2022, his campaign said that he had asked his publisher to correct the promotional text on The Other Wes Moore , and it did for later editions. Moore quickly learned to be more careful: “I’m not a Baltimorean by birth, but I’m a Baltimorean by choice,” he told a crowd in 2022. But a pattern had been established—or at least a line of attack. In 2010, Stephen Colbert described Moore, a guest on The Colbert Report , as a recipient of a Bronze Star for his service in Afghanistan, where he’d served in 2005 and 2006. The trouble was that he didn’t have a Bronze Star. When reporters raised questions about the medal, Moore’s staff insisted that he’d never told anyone that he had won it, and so he wasn’t responsible for the error. But in 2024, The New York Times obtained Moore’s application for a White House fellowship in 2006 in which he’d written, “the 82nd Airborne Division have awarded me the Bronze Star Medal.” He had an explanation for that too: The senior officer who had helped Moore write the application told him that he was going to get the medal, and so he should include it; the fact that it never actually arrived was embarrassing, but not unusual in the chaos of wartime. And after the controversy surfaced, the military did indeed award him a Bronze Star —just 18 years late. [ From the July 2026 issue: Being Black in Pete Hegseth’s military ] Then the Free Beacon ran a story questioning Moore’s account that his great-grandfather had moved to Jamaica because he’d been targeted by the KKK, based on the fact that reporters couldn’t find contemporaneous newspaper or archival accounts to verify it. This charge seemed more than a little forced—as did the many stories about Moore’s thesis at the University of Oxford. In that same White House fellowship application, he wrote that he’d received his degree in 2003 or 2004, but it wasn’t formally recorded until 2005. He also listed the title of his thesis as “The Rise and Ramifications of Radical Islam in the Western Hemisphere,” but it was later titled “Radical Islam in Latin America in the Late 20th Century and Its Middle Eastern Roots.” Also, the thesis is not stored in Oxford’s Bodleian Library—though there is no requirement for theses to be kept there, and many aren’t. Moore told The Baltimore Sun that he wasn’t “going to spend a second of my time trying to dig” a copy up. Marvin Joseph / The Washington Post / Getty Moore officially receives the Bronze Star Medal in 2024. If you’re a little bored, you’re right to be. Some people have compared Moore to Barack Obama, and the demands for him to release more records to back up his past inevitably reminded me of the “birther” conspiracy. At least that conspiracy had some stakes. How much should anyone care that in 2006, Moore said he’d been named to the Maryland College Football Hall of Fame when in fact he had been honored only by a College Football Hall of Fame affiliate called the National Football Foundation? Moore expresses regret for not being clear about the Bronze Star, but when I asked him about the attacks on his truthfulness in general, he dismissed them. “Do you know who has never attacked my military record? The United States Army,” he said. He told me he lived by a code: “You do not lie, cheat, or steal.” In fact, he said, he was being accused of dishonesty precisely because he was so honest. “It’s basic laws of warfare: You go after your opponent’s strength.” And he pointed out that these accusations surfaced only after he started gaining support. “I went a whole year on a campaign, and no one had a word to say about me,” he said. “And then out of nowhere, it was like the deluge began,” and people from “the right wing started putting stuff out.” The Baltimore Sun , which has devoted much space to these controversies, has indeed moved rightward under a new owner, the television magnate David Smith, and the conservative Free Beacon ’s tagline is a promise to cover “the enemies of freedom in the way the mainstream media won’t.” Moore told me that Obama had given him advice on surviving these kinds of attacks as a politician, saying, “Listen, this is the part of the game that everyone hates.” But if the questions about Moore’s honesty have been amplified by his opponents, they still trace back to an uncomfortable set of facts: Moore allowed people to call him a Bronze Star–winning Baltimore kid, when the story was more complicated. In April, one of Moore’s biggest legislative priorities—a redistricting plan that could have helped Democrats pick up a seat in the midterms—died when William Ferguson, the Democratic president of the state Senate, refused to bring it up for a vote. It was “ too risky ,” Ferguson argued: The new map could be challenged, and a ruling could leave their party worse off. Ferguson is now pushing to get a constitutional amendment before Maryland voters in November that would better shore up any new map from legal challenges. Moore has framed the legislature’s caution as timidity, but Ferguson has a different take. He told me that Moore had created confusion by waiting months before coming out in favor of the plan, and suggested that the governor embraced it only after Gavin Newsom gained national attention for pushing through a new map in California. “I don’t think that timing was a coincidence,” Ferguson said, adding that Moore tends to emphasize “messaging” over governing. “Comms is dictating policy, and policy is not dictating comms.” He did, however, credit Moore with working to speedily rebuild the Francis Scott Key Bridge. Its collapse, in 2024, killed six people and is the most significant catastrophe Moore has weathered as governor. The port of Baltimore was expected to be shut down for many months, but the state got it open again after less than three. Chip Somodevilla / Getty Governor Moore speaking at a commemoration ceremony at the Francis Scott Key Bridge, March, 2025. Moore is expected to win a second term in November, but the public’s mistrust has taken a political toll. The Sun and others have accused him of not being forthcoming about the state’s budget, which has seesawed from deficit to surplus to deficit again during his tenure. His vetoing of the reparations bill made some of his core supporters feel that he had misled them. When Moore’s approval rating declined, poll respondents listed the budget and the governor’s trustworthiness among their top concerns. Something about Moore does feel protean . He’s hard to place. His background can be confusing. Although he’s often compared to Obama, his education was far less rarefied. Obama was the president of the Harvard Law Review ; Moore went to junior college before landing at Johns Hopkins. He describes his upbringing as working-class—“a very hardworking family, but it was definitely a working-class family.” Perhaps by income, but by few other definitions. Both parents were college graduates. His father was an anchorman at a radio station and his mother wrote for radio and TV. Although Moore frequently says that she didn’t have a job with benefits until he was a teenager, she had won a Peabody Award and taught journalism at Howard University before he was born. Still, he saw himself as an outsider, and wouldn’t invite his friends from Riverdale back to his neighborhood. He told me that he thought very strategically about fitting in: “Okay, how do I adapt and adjust so I don’t stick out?” At Valley Forge, he was taught how to mingle with the powerful—how to walk, eat, and speak. As a high-ranking cadet, he attended lunches with former presidents, including Gerald Ford and George H. W. Bush. He said he eventually learned to accept that he was different and to be “comfortable in my own skin.” In two separate conversations, he quoted the same Jay-Z line: “I’m comfortable, dog, Brooklyn to Rome.” But he enunciated every word, in a way that sounded stiff. Despite his charisma onstage, up close, he has no swag. Where he seemed most at home was at the matcha café in Baltimore owned by an old friend of his, who surprised him with a Jamaican sorrel—a tart iced drink. “This right here would make my grandmother proud,” he said. Once, I made a Bernie Mac reference, and he got it immediately, and we shared a knowing laugh. Above all, he was comfortable talking about religion. “I come from a whole long line of preachers and teachers,” he said. “My great-grandfather was a minister; my grandfather was a minister.” In the summers, he used to stay in his grandfather’s parsonage in Brooklyn. When he told his grandmother that he was running for office, she said, “When you’re done with that, maybe you can become a minister.” “Asking me not to talk about or to acknowledge God is like asking me not to breathe air,” he told me. Don Smallwood for The Atlantic When I asked his mother, Joy Moore, if she thought he would run for president, she said: “I think his faith will take him wherever he’s going to eventually go.” She seemed more annoyed by the questions about his honesty and integrity than Moore was. “They question things that are so personal,” she said. She felt as if the articles interrogating their family history were accusing them all—her grandfather, her father, herself, her son—of being liars. And the Oxford thesis? “I mean, if he knew he was going to one day run for governor, don’t you think he would have kept stuff like that?” [ Read: Something is happening in the Democratic base ] Moore says he’d had no plans to go into politics before 2022. It was his wife, Dawn, who was the political operative, a campaign strategist who’d worked for two lieutenant governors. She and Moore eloped when he was on leave from his service in Afghanistan. While they were dating, she was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, and I was curious about whether she found divulging it to him hard. After all, I know plenty of men who wouldn’t stick around for the common cold. She said she asked him: “How would you feel if you had to take care of me for the rest of your life?” And he said: “How would you feel, if you had to take care of me for the rest of my life?” Some of the questions regarding Moore’s authenticity amount to a nebulous discomfort with how he comes across, a discomfort I recognize from all the times I’ve encountered it myself. Many people who work in elite careers after growing up relatively disadvantaged, as well as Black people who spend time in primarily white spaces, are accused of not being true to themselves. This is a false dichotomy. We can be true to ourselves while also understanding that success requires us to be supple and adaptable, and to present different aspects of our personalities at different times. There’s a famous poem by Paul Laurence Dunbar called “ We Wear the Mask ,” about the way Black Americans shield themselves from racism. I mentioned it to Moore, and he recognized it immediately. “The mask is heavy,” he said. Moore says he wears his own mask around many people, “not because it makes me more comfortable—it’s because it makes them more comfortable.” Being in spaces where people are “not used to seeing you” is a burden, he said. Being “an enigma” is a burden. “To some people, your presence is inspirational. To certain people, your presence is offensive. To certain people, your presence means progress. To certain people, your presence means we’ve lost something.” You’re a first, or you’re a threat. “That weight does sit on you,” he said. “And it’s heavy.”

items.title: NACOC urges public support in fight against illicit drug trafficking
items.description: The Deputy Director of the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC), Alexander Barimah Twum, has called on the public to provide authorities with relevant information to help combat illicit drug trafficking in Ghana. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Monday, July 27, during a discussion on drug abuse among Ghanaians, particularly the youth, Mr Barimah Twum said public cooperation was critical to the success of efforts to tackle the drug menace. He expressed concern that some individuals had chosen to collaborate with drug dealers instead of reporting their activities to the appropriate authorities. According to him, such actions undermine the fight against illicit drugs and allow criminal networks to continue operating. Mr Barimah Twum urged the public to change this attitude by supporting law enforcement agencies with timely information on individuals involved in drug trafficking and related activities. “If citizens are able to open to us, if citizens are able to expose these evil doers, we can get to the root of this problem,” he said. “But when we get citizens conniving with them (illicit drug dealers), when we get citizens aiding and abetting this crime, it makes the work very difficult,” he added. He stressed that collective efforts from authorities and citizens were needed to address the growing challenges associated with drug abuse and trafficking in the country.

items.title: Communiqué: Digital Economy Forum calls for urgent action to protect public trust in Ghana’s cash-lite economy
items.description: Ghana’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem is facing a serious test of public confidence as fraud, social engineering and weak coordination across platforms threaten the country’s cash-lite agenda. This was the central issue at the inaugural Digital Economy Forum, convened by JoyNews and the Multimedia Group in partnership with Hubtel under the theme “The Trust Crisis: Why Fraud is Holding Back Ghana’s Digital Economy”. The forum brought together regulators, banks, fintech operators, mobile money providers, cybersecurity experts, academia, agents, students and members of the public for a documentary-led national dialogue on fraud and digital trust. Data presented at the forum showed that Ghana now has more than 80 million registered mobile money accounts, with over 26 million active accounts every 90 days. In 2025 alone, digital financial transactions reached nearly 10 billion in volume, valued at more than GH¢4.5 trillion. But participants warned that the same growth has created new vulnerabilities, with fraudsters increasingly targeting consumers through impersonation, phishing, fake customer service numbers, clone websites and other manipulative schemes. The forum recommended stronger industry-wide coordination, including the onboarding of fintechs and dedicated electronic money issuers onto the FinSec Security Operations Centre, the creation of a unified fintech and PSP association, stronger real-time fraud intelligence sharing, improved public education and better training for frontline police officers. Participants agreed that Ghana’s digital economy can only grow sustainably if secure technology is matched by informed consumers, faster incident response and stronger accountability across the financial ecosystem. items.title: Burkina: plus de 1,31 million de PDI ont regagné leur localités d’origine
items.description: (Ouagadougou, le 24 juillet 2026) L'un des principaux enseignements de l'évaluation à mi-parcours du contrat d'objectifs 2026 du Ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité demeure la dynamique encourageante de retour des personnes déplacées internes dans leurs localités d'origine. Au 30 juin 2026, plus de 1 310 000 personnes avaient regagné 1 034 localités, contre 1 160 000 personnes dans 871 localités au 31 décembre 2025. Cette évolution traduit l'amélioration progressive de la situation dans plusieurs zones du pays ainsi que les efforts déployés par le Gouvernement pour accompagner le retour des populations. Ce contexte a conduit le Camarade Premier Ministre à donner une orientation majeure au Ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité: Privilégier désormais la réhabilitation des habitations dans les villages de retour plutôt que la construction de logements dans les sites de déplacement, afin de consolider durablement la réinstallation des populations. Cette dynamique est accompagnée par plusieurs initiatives structurantes, notamment le renforcement des capacités du Conseil national de secours d’urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) avec l’acquisition de 68 camions, la campagne nationale Dèmè Sira, le lancement de sa plateforme numérique ainsi que la phase pilote du Service social mobile. Pour le Camarade Ministre toutes ces actions traduisent la volonté du Ministère d’aller au-delà de l’assistance d’urgence pour promouvoir le relèvement, la résilience et l’autonomisation des communautés. Elle a réaffirmé son engagement à poursuivre cette dynamique aux côtés de l'ensemble des partenaires afin que chaque famille retournée retrouve progressivement des conditions de vie dignes et durables. The second-fastest man in Ghana’s history produced a season’s best time of 10.00 seconds to win Heat 5 in commanding fashion, booking automatic qualification for Tuesday’s semi-finals. Azamati joins compatriot Abdul-Rasheed Saminu in the semis of the competition, with both Ghanaian sprinters among the leading contenders for the Commonwealth title. items.title: Gov’t dismisses claims over viral Mahama video, says remarks were taken out of context
items.description: The government has dismissed claims circulating on social media regarding a viral video of President John Dramani Mahama, describing them as false and a deliberate attempt to misrepresent his comments. The Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, issued the clarification in a Facebook post on Monday, July 27, following the widespread circulation of the video. According to Mr Kwakye Ofosu, the President’s remarks were taken out of context by what he described as “misguided elements” seeking to create a false narrative for partisan purposes. “Some misguided elements have sought to distort the President’s words in this video to achieve narrow partisan ends,” he stated. He explained that President Mahama was speaking about the release of GH¢150 million to support post-flood mitigation efforts during a meeting with the National Security Coordinator. Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the President’s reference to the release of funds was specifically related to government’s response to the impact of recent floods and not for any other purpose. “The President clearly speaks of the ‘release’ of GHS 150 million, which was in direct reference to funds for post-flood mitigation works. That is what he was discussing with the National Security Coordinator and nothing more,” he said. He urged the public to disregard what he described as misleading interpretations of the video, insisting that the claims were intended to spread misinformation. “Disregard the mischievous lies!” he added.

items.title: Asiedu Nketia and Ato Forson in dead heat for NDC leadership ahead of 2028 – Poll
items.description: The race to lead the National Democratic Congress (NDC) into the 2028 general elections is currently a close contest between the party’s National Chairman, Johnson Asiedu Nketia, and Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Baah Forson, according to a new poll by GlobalInfo Analytics. The survey, released on July 27, showed both potential candidates tied at 31 per cent among voters as the preferred choice to lead the NDC in 2028. This is not the first time a survey has suggested that the race is largely between the two leading figures of the party. This new poll indicated that Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu follows with 15 per cent support, while Vice President Prof. Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang received 9 per cent. Chief of Staff Julius Debrah polled 8 per cent, with Agriculture Minister Eric Opoku and Prof. Joshua Alabi each recording 2 per cent. The survey also projected possible outcomes for the 2028 presidential election, with Dr Ato Forson emerging as the frontrunner in a hypothetical contest involving candidates from the major political parties. According to the poll, if Dr Ato Forson contests against former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia, Kennedy Agyapong, Alan Kyeremanten and Nana Kwame Bediako, he would secure 57.5 per cent of the votes. Dr Bawumia would obtain 35.3 per cent, followed by Kennedy Agyapong with 4.3 per cent, Nana Kwame Bediako with 0.6 per cent and Alan Kyeremanten with 0.5 per cent. Other candidates accounted for 1.8 per cent. In another scenario where Johnson Asiedu Nketia replaces Dr Ato Forson as the NDC candidate, the poll showed the NDC National Chairman leading with 54.2 per cent. Dr Bawumia would receive 37.1 per cent, while Kennedy Agyapong, Alan Kyeremanten and Nana Kwame Bediako would poll 4.8 per cent, 1.0 per cent and 0.8 per cent respectively. Other candidates accounted for 2.1 per cent. The GlobalInfo Analytics survey was conducted through telephone interviews between July 15 and 24, 2026, involving 7,761 voters across all 16 regions of Ghana. The poll, which forms part of a longitudinal study, has a confidence level of 99 per cent and a margin of error of plus or minus 1.5 per cent.

items.title: Poni: La commune de Gaoua renforce le dialogue avec les citoyens à travers une journée de redevabilité
items.description: BURKINA-PONI-JOURNEE-REDEVABILITE Poni: La commune de Gaoua renforce le dialogue avec les citoyens à travers une journée de redevabilité Gaoua, 23 juil. 2026 (AIB) – La délégation spéciale de la commune de Gaoua a organisé, le jeudi 23 juillet 2026, une journée de dialogue et de redevabilité consacrée à la présentation du bilan de sa gestion 2025. Cette rencontre a permis aux autorités communales, aux acteurs de la société civile et aux populations d'échanger sur les réalisations enregistrées et les défis à relever pour un développement local. Selon le président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Gaoua, Siaka Ouattara, cette initiative vise à renforcer la transparence dans la gestion communale et à consolider la confiance entre les gestionnaires de la collectivité et les citoyens. « Il faut qu'à un moment donné de la gestion de la commune, nous fassions une halte pour faire le point afin de permettre aux uns et aux autres de comprendre ce qui est fait. Cela permet de renforcer davantage la confiance entre les gestionnaires et la population », a-t-il expliqué. Pour lui, cette journée a permis de présenter les principales actions réalisées au cours de l'année 2025, notamment des investissements destinés à renforcer les capacités financières et économiques de la commune ainsi que la réalisation d'infrastructures structurantes et marchandes au profit des populations. « Toutes ces réalisations visent à impulser davantage le développement au niveau local », a-t-il indiqué, réaffirmant la volonté des autorités communales de poursuivre les efforts engagés au bénéfice des populations. Cette journée de dialogue et de redevabilité traduit la volonté de la commune de Gaoua de promouvoir une gouvernance locale participative fondée sur la transparence, le dialogue et l'implication citoyenne au service du développement durable de la collectivité. items.title: Wings Over the Sahel: Why Ghana and West Africa must build a drone-ready security doctrine
items.description: On the night I spent exploring the town of Elubo for my story “In the Dark: The security risk Ghana is ignoring at Elubo” , what surprised me most was not the complaints from community members about the unseen illegal crossings but rather the dark stretches of frontier that no patrol vehicle, no checkpoint lights, and no border guard could realistically cover. Ghana’s land borders alone stretch for more than 2,090 km, running through forests and waterways that were never designed with modern security in mind. That exposure left me with an uncomfortable question that has only grown louder in the months since: how does a country with limited manpower and an overstretched budget monitor a border it cannot physically patrol? The answer being adopted from Kyiv to Bamako is the same. You put eyes and firepower in the sky where needed. This is not a hypothetical scenario. It is already taking place on the continent. Jihadist groups such as Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) have been documented flying kamikaze drones deep within the Sahel, and their reach now extends to the borders of Togo, Ivory Coast, and Benin. In January 2026, an Islamic State affiliate reportedly used kamikaze drones in a single coordinated assault on Niamey’s international airport in Niger. Benin recorded its deadliest jihadist attack in years, roughly 300 kilometres from Accra. The war Ghanaians regarded as someone else’s, playing out from a distance on screen, is now drawing near with drones. What Ukraine Has Taught the World About Drone Warfare Nowhere has the transformative power of drones been more clearly demonstrated than in the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year. A 2026 study by Dr. Fred P. Hoffman, Dr. Behsat Ekici, and Brock Ruth of Mercyhurst University’s Intelligence Studies Department, published in the Croatian defence journal Strategos, asks a very important question every security agency on the continent should also be asking: does the evolution of drone warfare in Ukraine amount to a mere revolution in military affairs (RMA) or a full military revolution (MR)? The difference is worth making here. A revolution in military affairs (RMA), the authors explain, refers to technological, tactical, doctrinal, or organisational changes confined to the military sphere. New weapons used in familiar ways. A military revolution goes further: it redefines not just how wars are fought, but how militaries are organised and how states themselves function. Citing the Pentagon strategist Andrew Krepinevich’s four criteria: technological change, military systems evolution, operational innovation, and organisational adaptation — Hoffman, Ekici, and Ruth conclude, based on interviews with ten drone-warfare specialists across Western militaries and intelligence services, that Ukraine’s experience meets all four. In other words, drone warfare is not a passing trend. It represents a genuine revolution, on the scale of the machine gun in WWI or the aircraft carrier in WWII. The figures backing this up are striking. Ukraine reportedly manufactured about 2.2 million small first-person-view (FPV) drones in 2024 alone, plus around 100,000 larger long-range models, with most of the ones used by its troops domestically manufactured. These first-person-view drones, which cost just $500, now account for a large share of Russian casualties. The Strategos study puts it near 80 percent, making them deadlier than artillery on the battlefield. A Ukrainian interceptor drone built for roughly $1,600 has been used to shoot down Russian reconnaissance drones worth tens of thousands of dollars each. As one Kyiv-based electronic-warfare executive quoted in the study put it, a single guided missile can cost a million dollars and kill a dozen people, but that same amount buys ten thousand drones capable of far more damage. This is the math that should concern every security agency in Africa. It is exactly the math that Sahelian jihadist groups are continually exploiting against forces that, in many cases, still rely on foot patrols and fixed checkpoints. Drones Do Not Just Win Wars— They Change How States Behave If Ukraine’s example demonstrates why drones are important on the battlefield, the newest and perhaps most important contribution to this topic explains something security agencies rarely stop to consider: how drones shape decision-making itself. In his 2025 book The Remote Revolution: Drones and Modern Statecraft, MIT political scientist Dr. Erik Lin-Greenberg overturns a widely held assumption that cheap, low-cost drones make leaders quicker to strike and push crises closer to war. Drawing on original wargames, survey experiments, and case studies of American and Israeli drone operations, Lin-Greenberg argues that because drone missions carry no risk of a pilot being captured or killed, they lower the political cost of using force, but that same low cost also makes those operations far less likely to spiral into wider, more intense conflict than a comparable mission flown by a drone would. In his view, drones add a new step to the escalation ladder, giving states a more convenient way to respond. He argues this amounts to nothing less than a revolution in how modern states conduct their affairs. For security agencies in West Africa, this should not be taken just as an academic point but as a policy tool in itself. A Ghanaian or Nigerian security service equipped with surveillance and light-strike drones would have graduated options for responding to a cross-border incursion or a smuggling convoy. These are options that do not require sending troops, risking soldiers’ lives, consuming time, or triggering a diplomatic incident with a neighbouring state. Lin-Greenberg’s research suggests the more likely outcome is drone-enabled restraint, provided the doctrine and command structure around the technology are solid. That is the one condition West African security agencies cannot afford to skip. The Threat Is Already at the Gate Fortunately, Ghana has not experienced any jihadist attacks like Mali, Burkina Faso, and increasingly Benin. Even though conflicts in Bawku and the north have flared up now and then, it has managed to prevent jihadist violence. Security analysts monitoring the Sahel warn that armed-drone use by militant groups is expected to keep expanding through 2026, with JNIM already the dominant user of armed drones in the region. It is expanding its activity into western and southern Burkina Faso and Mali, areas right on the border with Ghana, Ivory Coast, Togo, and Benin. The withdrawal of French and American forces from Niger, and the closure of a key Western drone and intelligence hub there, has left a vacuum that Sahelian juntas have filled with a patchwork of alternative partners: drones sourced from the UAE, training support from Morocco, and other ad hoc arrangements. Western countries have moved to what is now described as an “over-the-horizon” strategy. Instead of focusing on the Sahel’s interior, they’re now backing coastal countries like Ghana, Ivory Coast, and Benin as the new front line. Ghana and its coastal neighbours now need stronger drone and surveillance abilities of their own, instead of relying on outside support due to this new shift. Turning the Lessons Into Policy This does not mean turning Ghana’s security architecture into a smaller replica of the Ukrainian battlefield. Instead, it means being more careful and disciplined. That is, adapting the proven lessons of Ukraine’s drone revolution and the strategic thinking of Lin-Greenberg’s escalation research and turning them into an approach that fits West Africa’s actual threats: border crossings by armed groups, communal violence, clashes linked to illegal mining (galamsey), piracy in the Gulf of Guinea, and extremism spreading south from the Sahel. What we’ve seen points to several concrete steps. – Layered aerial surveillance of the northern border regions (Upper East, Upper West, and Savannah), using low-cost fixed-wing and quadcopter reconnaissance drones to close the blind stretches that undercut checkpoint-based patrolling. – A domestic drone-assembly and maintenance capacity, rather than reliance on costly imported systems, following Ukraine’s example of building a low-cost, locally serviceable fleet rather than a small number of expensive, hard-to-replace platforms. – Investment in counter-drone and electronic-warfare capability, since the same technology available to Ghana’s security services is equally available and increasingly used by armed groups and criminal networks operating along the borders. – Clear rules of engagement and command authority for drone use, so that the flexibility Lin-Greenberg identifies as de-escalatory is preserved by doctrine and does not collapse into unaccountable or indiscriminate use. – Regional intelligence-sharing on drone sightings and incidents among Ghana, Ivory Coast, Togo, and Benin, mirroring the cross-border coordination that has allowed jihadist groups themselves to operate across borders. – Dedicated training pipelines for drone operators and analysts, building the kind of specialised, rapidly-trainable workforce that Ukraine’s drone schools have shown can be stood up quickly and cheaply relative to conventional pilot training. The Cost of Waiting Security agencies often judge how ready they are by counting personnel and vehicles. But Ukraine’s experience and the growing drone threat spreading from the Sahel toward Ghana’s border show that this way of measuring readiness is outdated. A border can now be breached without anyone crossing it in person; it can be surveilled and struck from several kilometres away by an enemy who never sets foot on the ground. West African security agencies that continue to plan primarily around foot patrols and manned aircraft will end up as Ukrainian and Sahelian forces already have, outpaced by enemies who adapted first. The good news is that this is one of the few areas in modern defence where getting started does not cost too much. Unlike fighter jets or navy ships, building real drone capability doesn’t need massive spending programs. What it needs is a clear strategy and a local system for maintaining and building the equipment. Not forgetting the political will to treat drones as a core part of national security. Ghana and West Africa have a good reason and growing chance to build this capability now before the threat fully arrives. The kilometres between Burkina Faso and Accra used to be seen as a safe distance. Today, as this piece has shown, they should be seen as a warning instead and as a window of time that’s still open to invest in smart and low-cost drone security before that window closes on us.

items.title: 42 percent of Ghanaians disagree with Abu Trica extradition decision — GlobalInfo Analytics poll
items.description: A new survey by GlobalInfo Analytics has revealed that 42 per cent of Ghanaian voters disagree with the government’s decision to extradite Fredrick Kumi, popularly known as “Abu Trica”, to the United States (USA) before the completion of his appeal process. Earlier this month, the High Court in Accra approved the extradition of Abu Trica to the USA , where he is wanted to stand trial over an alleged romance fraud scheme said to involve approximately US$8 million. According to the poll, released on 27 July, 29 per cent of respondents agreed with the government’s action, while another 29 per cent said they had no opinion on the matter. The findings come amid public debate over the circumstances surrounding Abu Trica’s extradition to the USA to face criminal charges, particularly concerns over whether due process was followed before the appeal process against his extradition was concluded. According to the survey, a larger proportion of respondents expressed disapproval of the government’s decision compared to those who supported it, highlighting mixed public sentiments on the matter. Meanwhile, the poll also assessed Ghanaians’ views on the country’s relationship with global powers. The survey found that Canada is the global power viewed most favourably by Ghanaians, recording a net favourability rating of 38 points. China followed with 34 points, while the United Kingdom received a rating of 33 points. The European Union recorded 22 points, with the United States scoring 7 points. South Africa recorded the lowest favourability rating among the countries assessed, with a net rating of negative 61 points. Russia followed with negative 6 points, while another country listed in the poll recorded negative 3 points. The survey was a longitudinal telephone interview carried out from 15th to 24th July 2026 with a sample of 7,761 voters from all 16 regions in Ghana. The poll has a confidence level of 99% and a margin of error of ±1.5%.

items.title: Burkina Faso : La 1ʳᵉ édition du « Festival Boulgou » célèbre la culture bissa et la cohésion sociale à Garango
items.description: La ville de Garango, dans la région du Nakambé, a vibré du 23 au 25 juillet 2026 au rythme de la première édition du « Festival Boulgou ». Initiée par Jules Bambara, cette manifestation dédiée à la promotion de la culture bissa s'est refermée en présence des autorités administratives, coutumières, religieuses et des représentants des parrains. Le Haut-Commissaire de la province du Boulgou, Domèbèguirè Constantin Dabiré, représentant le gouverneur de la région du Nakambé, a procédé à la clôture de cette première édition du Festival Boulgou au soir du samedi 25 juillet 2026, sur le terrain de Bougoula à Garango. Durant trois jours, le « bissako » (la culture bissa) a été valorisé dans sa richesse et sa diversité à travers des danses traditionnelles, des contes, des jeux ancestraux, des prestations artisanales et le savoir-faire local. « « Festival Boulgou » est l’appellation choisie pour cette manifestation par respect aux sacrifices faits au mont Boulgou une fois par an, regroupant des milliers de personnes », a expliqué le promoteur. En rappel, le mont Boulgou est la colline sacrée qui a donné son nom à la province. Dans son allocution, le promoteur a souligné que le festival répond à la dynamique actuelle du gouvernement burkinabè visant à valoriser les savoirs endogènes. Il a ajouté qu’au-delà de son caractère festif, cet événement constitue un cadre de promotion du tourisme local, de soutien aux acteurs culturels, de valorisation des artisans, de promotion des produits locaux et de dynamisation de l’économie provinciale. Le festival a d’ailleurs servi de cadre à une exposition foraine au profit des festivaliers. Jules Bambara, Promoteur du Festival Boulgou Le camarade Birba, Directeur régional de la Construction et de la Patrie du Nakambé, représentant les parrains, le camarade Ministre des Mines et des Carrières et le camarade Directeur général de la LONAB, a quant à lui invité la jeunesse à retourner aux sources. Il a salué la pluie torrentielle tombée avant la clôture, y voyant la réponse des ancêtres aux sacrifices qui leur ont été faits. La soirée a également été marquée par des prestations d’artistes locaux mettant en valeur le style tradi-moderne et par la remise de prix aux gagnants des différentes compétitions. Le camarade Haut-Commissaire, patron de la cérémonie, a félicité le promoteur pour la réussite de l’initiative. « À travers la mise en valeur de la culture bissa, notamment par la musique et la gastronomie, vous avez su magnifier notre identité et renforcer les liens de fraternité entre les fils et filles du Boulgou » , a-t-il déclaré, avant d'ajouter : « Ce festival a démontré une fois de plus que la culture est un puissant levier de cohésion sociale, de paix et de développement local ». Les festivaliers venus de toutes parts ont exprimé leur satisfaction, à l’instar de Zaliatou Zeba, venue de Sanogo. « Je suis très contente d'être ici et j’encourage de telles initiatives, car elles rassemblent. », a-t-elle confié. Quant au jeune Olivier Lompo, venu en famille, il a confié : « Je suis très content parce qu’il y a du monde, je veux revenir ici l’an prochain ». Durant trois jours d’affilée, la ville de Garango a vécu au rythme du « bissako », l’expression de la fierté du peuple bissa. En synergie, le camarade Haut-Commissaire et le camarade Président de la Délégation spéciale ont formulé le vœu que les prochaines éditions soient encore plus ambitieuses et rayonnantes. items.title: 2026 Commonwealth Games: Saminu books semifinal spot in men’s 100m
items.description: Ghana’s Abdul-Rasheed Saminu has booked his place in the men’s 100m semi-finals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games after an impressivevictory in his opening heat on Monday. The Ghanaian national record holder clocked a season’s best time of 10.01 seconds to finish first, comfortably ahead of Orphee Topize of Mauritius and Mc Kish Comptonof St Vincent and the Grenadines. Saminu, who is among the favourites for the men’s 100m title, delivered a composed performance to secure automatic qualification and strengthen his medal ambitions. He will return to the track on Tuesday for the semi-finals, where he will be aiming to maintain his impressive form and move a step closer to the Commonwealth crown.

items.title: Los incendios de Madrid, Ávila y Toledo afectan ya a 77.000 hectáreas y obligan a evacuar o confinar a 90.000 personas
items.description: Los incendios forestales que arrasan la provincia de Ávila y la Comunidad de Madrid siguen activos , aunque su avance es más lento. La extinción está siendo compleja y se ha visto dificultada por las fuertes rachas de viento. Tras varias jornadas de rápido avance, el domingo se lograron contener muchos de los frentes, aunque se mantienen activas “varias cabezas” y los fuegos no pueden darse por perimetrados. Los esfuerzos este lunes se centran precisamente en esas “cabezas” y en intentar lograr su estabilización , al mismo tiempo que se protegen las poblaciones y se evita una fusión de las llamas de los dos grandes focos. Un ataque coordinado contra los puntos que arden con más voracidad. La evolución es positiva, pero muy lenta y el riesgo de reactivaciones es alto. La Unidad Militar de Emergencias (UME) los gestiona como un solo incendio y el Gobierno amplió la emergencia nacional a Toledo, donde inquieta un nuevo fuego en Almorox. Entre las tres regiones, hay afectadas ya 77.000 hectáreas y alrededor de 90.000 evacuados o confinados. Solo en Ávila, son 50.000 hectáreas, lo que lo convierte en el mayor incendio y “el más agresivo” de la historia de España. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Dansa Kourouma aux sages de la Basse-Guinée : « Si nous nous trompons, dites-nous que ce n’est pas bon »
items.description: Le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Dr Dansa Kourouma, a reçu, dimanche, 26 juillet, à son domicile privé de Somaya, dans la commune de Manéah (Coyah), une importante délégation des sages de la Basse-Guinée, conduite par le Kountigui, Elhadj Souna Yansané. Selon les proches du président de l’Assemblée nationale, cette délégation était venue le féliciter à la suite de son choix consensuel, le 17 juillet dernier, à la tête de l’Assemblée nationale, deuxième institution de la République. À cette occasion, les sages de la Basse-Guinée ont réitéré leur soutien à Dr Dansa Kourouma et l’ont encouragé à poursuivre ses efforts au service de la République et de l’ensemble des Guinéens. En retour, le président du Parlement a remercié la délégation et l’a invitée à prier pour le président de la République, rappelant que « lorsque le chef n’est pas à l’aise, le pays ne peut pas l’être non plus ». Il a également demandé des prières pour les députés, afin que la 10ᵉ législature accomplisse sa mission avec succès, ainsi que pour la paix et la prospérité de la Guinée. « Si nous gâtons, si nous nous trompons et que vous ne nous en parlez pas, Dieu sera notre témoin. Si vous nous trouvez sur le mauvais chemin, dites-nous : “Ça, ce n’est pas bon.” », a déclaré, en langue soussou, Dr Dansa Kourouma. Figure bien connue de la société civile guinéenne, Dr Dansa Kourouma a présidé le Conseil national de la transition (CNT) depuis sa mise en place par le CNRD, avant d’être porté à la tête de l’Assemblée nationale. Christine Finda KOUROUMA L’article Dansa Kourouma aux sages de la Basse-Guinée : « Si nous nous trompons, dites-nous que ce n’est pas bon » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: AES : La Force unifiée montera en puissance de 5 000 à 18 000 soldats
items.description: La Confédération des États du Sahel (AES) s’apprête à muscler son dispositif sécuritaire. Lors d’un entretien accordé le samedi 26 juillet 2026 à la télévision nationale nigérienne, le Général d’armée Abdourahamane Tiani, président du Niger, a annoncé que les effectifs de la Force unifiée de l’AES passeront progressivement de 5 000 à 18 000 soldats. Cette montée en puissance, décidée par les ministres de la Défense du Burkina Faso, du Mali et du Niger, s’inscrit dans une stratégie de renforcement des capacités militaires de la Confédération. L’objectif est de répondre avec davantage d’efficacité à la menace terroriste qui frappe l’espace sahélien. Installé à Niamey, l’état-major opérationnel de la Force unifiée est déjà opérationnel et a mené plusieurs interventions sur le terrain. Sans entrer dans le détail de ces actions, le chef de l’État nigérien a rappelé que les impératifs de sécurité imposent une discrétion stricte sur les plans et les opérations militaires en cours. « Nous voulons atteindre 18 000 hommes car nous mesurons pleinement l’ampleur des défis auxquels nous sommes confrontés », a déclaré Abdourahamane Tiani, à l’occasion d’un bilan des deux premières années d’existence de la Confédération des États du Sahel. Ce renforcement progressif traduit la volonté de l’AES de bâtir une défense commune plus solide et d’approfondir la coopération militaire entre ses trois membres dans la lutte contre le terrorisme. Minute.bf

items.title: India's Cockroach Janta Party demands release of protesters after reports of detention
items.description: India’s youth-led “cockroach” movement, whose protests have forced the education minister’s resignation, urged authorities on Monday to release all demonstrators detained in weeks of rallies nationwide . The online Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which organised protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said they had received reports of students held in detention, particularly in the states of Assam, West Bengal and Bihar. “Any failure to release those detained or withdraw criminal cases would amount to a breach of public trust,” the protest group said in a statement, adding they would take “further necessary steps” if their demand was not met. The statement comes two days after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister over repeated failures in the conduct of competitive exams that have fuelled anger among millions of young Indians. The CJP accused the government of backtracking after authorities had assured them that no punitive action would be taken against protesters. The movement has won millions of followers on social media since it was launched in May by 30-year-old public relations graduate Abhijeet Dipke. It emerged initially as a satirical response to Chief Justice Surya Kant reportedly likening young people to “cockroaches” and “parasites” during a court hearing. The movement has since broadened its agenda to include concerns over unemployment, opportunities for young people and what it describes as Modi’s increasingly authoritarian style of governance. Tens of thousands of protesters, mainly students, rallied last week in New Delhi and other cities, demanding Pradhan’s resignation and broader reforms of the examination system. Demonstrations in the Indian capital turned violent on July 20 when a crowd attempted to march towards parliament from the Jantar Mantar protest site. Police fired tear gas and used batons to disperse the protest, triggering clashes and a wave of detentions. The protests have emerged as one of the biggest challenges to Modi since his re-election for a third term in office in 2024. The issue reverberated in parliament on Monday, with repeated disruptions as opposition lawmakers demanded a response from the government over last week’s police crackdown . Despite the disruptions, the government introduced legislation in the lower house seeking tougher penalties for examination paper leaks. A series of exam irregularities have undermined trust in India’s testing system, including the leak of a medical entrance question paper that forced more than two million candidates to retake the test. Another dispute involving the online marking of examinations taken by nearly two million high school students has further fuelled public anger.

items.title: Water supply to parts of Karachi resumes after power at Dhabeji pumping station restored
items.description: KARACHI: Water supply to several parts of Karachi resumed in phases on Monday after electricity supply was resumed at the Dhabeji pumping station, around 22 hours after a power breakdown, Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation spokesperson Abdul Qadir Shaikh told Dawn . The spokesperson said K-Electric (KE) had restored power supply to the pumping station at 7:20am on Monday, around 22 hours after a cable fault suspended the supply at 8:43am on Sunday. He said the “prolonged outage had resulted in a shortfall of nearly 48 million gallons of water in the city” and the affected areas included parts of North Nazimabad, Nazimabad, Gulberg Town, New Karachi, Landhi, Korangi and Scheme 33. “Following the restoration of electricity, water supply to the affected areas has resumed in phases,” the spokesperson said. The Dhabeji pumping station, Karachi’s primary water intake point, is highly dependent on uninterrupted electricity. Even brief outages result in immediate service disruptions. The power breakdown on Sunday had resulted in the temporary shutdown of three pumps at Dhabeji, which KWSC initially attributed to a cable fault. The water utility’s spokesperson had told Dawn that a technical team had reached the site to rectify the fault. However, a KE spokesperson had clarified that the fault in KDA Pumping Feeder 2, which supplies electricity to the Dhabeji Pumping Station, “is internal in nature and is not related to K-Electric”. “Power supply to 19 out of 22 pumping motors at the Dhabeji Pumping Station is continuing as normal,” the spokesperson had said, adding that a power utility team was in contact with the relevant authorities to assist KWSC in addressing the fault. On Monday, after the power was restored, the KWSC official said while speaking to Dawn that the electricity supply had been disconnected due to a cable fault, and whether the fault in KE’s cable was internal or external, it was the power utility’s responsibility to rectify it. Dawn reached out to KE for further details, but there was no immediate response. Earlier this month, an electricity outage at Dhabeji had affected its K-2 Pump House, where the manifold chamber and main valves developed a fault. As a result, three major pumps at the K-2 Pumping Station had been temporarily shut down and water supply to several areas of Karachi was affected. Last month, on June 1, supply from Hub Pumping Station was also suspended to parts of Karachi due to a fault in KE’s main cable. KWSC said that the power suspension had resulted in a daily water shortfall of 85 million gallons per day (MGD) for the city. It was the third consecutive day of power failures at key pumping stations disrupting distribution across the metropolis. On May 31, the city faced a shortfall of 122 MGD after electricity supply to the North East Karachi Pumping Station was disrupted due to a fault in K-Electric’s main cable. The outage came just a day after an emergency shutdown at the Dhabeji Pumping Station, caused by a fault in a transformer at the grid station, forced 10 of the station’s 21 pumping units to shut down.

items.title: Oil prices sink as US-Iran pause fuels fresh Hormuz hopes
items.description: Oil prices tumbled on Monday as a pause in tit-for-tat strikes between the United States and Iran boosted hopes for a return to their ceasefire and negotiations on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The United States held fire at the weekend after 13 days of attacks on sites in the Islamic republic, and Donald Trump’s UN envoy said the US president was “giving talks some space”. Tehran said in turn it would stop its retaliatory attacks on regional neighbours, handing Gulf shipping and the oil industry a respite. The two resumed hostilities this month, breaking a fragile truce, after Iran attacked ships passing through Omani waters in the Strait of Hormuz, sparking a pattern of escalation. That derailed diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran, but the conflict then expanded beyond the vital energy corridor when Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen hit Saudi vessels in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, a crucial passage into the Red Sea. Crude prices soared on the flare-up, with Brent breaking back above $100 a barrel last week for the first time since May. News that shipping continued in the Red Sea helped investors pare the gains on Friday. However, Trump’s decision to hold off on more strikes and Iran’s claims on Sunday that it had made progress in talks with Oman on management of the Strait of Hormuz provided some much-needed relief. The discussions focused on “common principles and operational mechanisms” for ensuring the safe passage of shipping through the strait while respecting the sovereign rights of the two states, Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said. A report also said mediator Pakistan was looking at resuming US-Iran peace talks, following a push initiated by China. Both main oil contracts sank on Monday, with Brent shedding more than seven percent at one point to briefly drop back below $90. “It looks as if developments in the Middle East have moved in a positive direction over the weekend, adding some credibility to the notion that oil above $100 a barrel seems to induce de-escalatory behaviour from both sides,” wrote National Australia Bank’s Sally Auld. – Inflation fears ease – The positive developments eased worries about a reignition of inflation and a fresh round of interest rate hikes, in turn helping equity markets higher. However, concerns about the sustainability of the AI boom and questions over the eye-watering sums pumped into the sector continue to dog traders, as tech firms bear the brunt of selling. Seoul, which has led the rout in recent weeks, rose one percent with chip giants SK hynix and Samsung enjoying some much-needed buying interest. Tokyo rose, though tech firms Advantest and Kioxia suffered more hefty selling pressure. Hong Kong, Sydney, Shanghai, Wellington, Singapore, Mumbai and Manila were also up. London, Paris and Frankfurt rose at the open. Taipei and Bangkok fell, while Jakarta was also in retreat following the surprise resignation of Indonesian central bank boss Perry Warjiyo citing personal reasons. Traders will be keenly awaiting the release of earnings from SK hynix, Samsung and Japan’s Kioxia this week, while US titans Microsoft, Meta, Apple and Amazon are also due, with focus on their outlooks and spending plans. Tim Waterer of KCM Trade said: “Traders remain somewhat nervy about the scale of the capex being committed, given lingering concerns over how long the return-on-investment phase may take to fully materialise.” Also in view this week is the Federal Reserve’s policy decision in light of the latest US-Iran flare-up and recent data indicating inflation easing. Bets on a hike have risen over the past week, though analysts expect officials to stand pat on Wednesday. However, Jenny Zeng at Allianz Global Investors warned: “While the (policy board) is likely to remain on hold in July, we continue to expect 50 basis points of tightening by year-end.” In company news, China’s leading memory chipmaker CXMT jumped 530 percent on its market debut in Shanghai to take it past megabank ICBC as the mainland’s most valuable company, before later paring the gains to end up 465 percent. The breathtaking surge came after the Anhui-based company had raised $9.8 billion in a blockbuster initial public offering, Bloomberg News reported, making it China’s biggest mainland tech share sale. – Key figures around 0810 GMT – West Texas Intermediate: DOWN 5.7 percent at $84.20 a barrel Brent North Sea Crude: DOWN 6.1 percent at $90.89 per barrel Tokyo – Nikkei 225: UP 0.5 percent at 64,931.19 (close) Hong Kong – Hang Seng Index: UP 1.0 percent at 25,207.18 (close) Shanghai – Composite: UP 1.2 percent at 3,858.24 (close) London – FTSE 100: UP 0.5 percent at 10,786.07 Euro/dollar: UP at $1.1400 from $1.1373 on Friday Pound/dollar: UP at $1.3341 from $1.3323 Euro/pound: UP at 85.45 pence from 85.34 pence Dollar/yen: DOWN at 163.46 yen from 163.84 New York – Dow: UP 0.5 percent at 51,947.25 (close) AFP The post Oil prices sink as US-Iran pause fuels fresh Hormuz hopes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: À El Ménéa, il verse de l’acide dans un abreuvoir pour empoisonner des dromadaires
items.description: Un agriculteur d’El Ménéa a choqué l'opinion publique en se faisant filmer en train d’empoisonner des bassins d’eau où s'abreuvent des dromadaires. Les autorités locales ont ouvert une enquête. La vidéo est devenue virale sur les réseaux sociaux et a suscité une vive indignation. El Ménéa : un agriculteur empoissonne des animaux avec de l’acide On y voit un agriculteur se plaindre des dromadaires qui paissent dans son champ de céréales, lui causant des pertes. Pour y remédier, il a eu recours à un procédé inacceptable : verser de l'acide dans deux bassins d'eau qui se trouvent à la lisière de la surface cultivée. Par ces fortes chaleurs, toute bête qui s’approche des lieux ne peut pas manquer de s’abreuvoir. “S’il y a une bête qui boit, je ne suis pas responsable”, dit-il en déversant le contenu de plusieurs bouteilles du liquide mortel. Des centaines de bêtes seraient mortes, selon des éleveurs D’autres vidéos ont vite suivi. Dans l'une d'entre elles, un éleveur assure que des centaines de camélidés sont morts dans la région du fait de ces pratiques. Les éleveurs nomades viennent de toutes les wilayas environnantes et même de l'extrême-sud, à la recherche de surfaces vertes pour leurs troupeaux. Si l'agriculteur a le droit de se plaindre des dégâts occasionnés à sa culture, ce qu'il a fait est unanimement condamné. Certains internautes ont qualifié son geste de crime contre la nature et les animaux. Une plainte a été déposée auprès de la justice Les autorités locales ont vite réagi. La direction des services agricoles (DSA) de la wilaya d’El Ménéa ont annoncé dans un communiqué qu'après de premières investigations, l’auteur de cet acte a été identifié. “Suite à la diffusion sur les réseaux sociaux (Facebook) d'une vidéo montrant une personne versant une substance acide dans l'eau destinée à l'abreuvement des animaux, nos investigations ont permis d'identifier l'individu responsable”, lit-on dans le communiqué. Les mêmes services ont annoncé qu'une plainte a été déposée auprès de la justice contre le suspect. “Notre objectif est de dissuader toute personne qui serait tentée de nuire au cheptel”, a indiqué la direction, assurant que “toutes les mesures nécessaires ont été prises pour éviter que de tels actes préjudiciables ne se répètent”. L’article À El Ménéa, il verse de l’acide dans un abreuvoir pour empoisonner des dromadaires est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: I’ll spend only four years in office, Obi insists
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has reaffirmed his commitment to serving only one term if elected president in the 2027 general election, insisting that four years would be enough to set Nigeria on the right path. Obi made the declaration during an interview on Channels TV Sunday Politics, dismissing suggestions that his one-term promise was merely a strategy to win power. Reacting to comments by his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, that both men had agreed Obi would serve only four years if elected, the former Anambra State governor said the arrangement was based on mutual trust. “I have said this thing several times. We have what we can call a meeting agreement. We are gentlemen; we must respect it. “I don’t need more than four years to show Nigerians the right path they will follow. It’s a simple thing. Even if you want me to sign it with you, I sign it with you. “A day more than four years is not Peter Obi. I want us to start trusting our leaders. When I was going to become a governor, I said the things that I would do, and when I came in, I started doing it. “I showed everybody. Go and listen to my campaign. I said I would manage their money efficiently. Schools will work; health works. Everything I said, I did. That is the way to work.” The post 2027: I’ll spend only four years in office, Obi insists appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Iran says summoned French envoy over ‘interference’ in internal affairs
items.description: Iran’s foreign ministry said on Monday it had summoned the French ambassador to Tehran to protest the conduct of two diplomats who were briefly detained earlier this month. “Yesterday, the French ambassador in Tehran was summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, where it was stressed that the French government must cease such actions and such interference in Iran’s internal affairs under misleading labels,” said the ministry’s spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing. He said the diplomats had “interfered in Iran’s internal affairs under the pretext of engaging with civil society”. Their actions, Baqaei said, were “in no way justified under the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations”. On July 20, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said two French diplomats in Iran were targeted by Iranian officials the day before and suffered “an extremely serious act of intimidation” by the Islamic republic’s security services. Both were “detained for several hours without reason, interrogated, and one of them was physically abused” before they were able to return to the embassy, he said. AFP The post Iran says summoned French envoy over ‘interference’ in internal affairs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 60% of Ghanaians say country is on right path, 72% approve Mahama’s performance – Survey
items.description: A majority of Ghanaian voters believe the country is heading in the right direction, while a significant number have expressed approval of President John Dramani Mahama’s performance, according to a new survey by GlobalInfo Analytics. The poll, released on July 27, found that 60 per cent of voters believe Ghana is moving in the right direction, while 28 per cent said the country is heading in the wrong direction. Another 12 per cent said they had no opinion. The survey also showed strong approval for President Mahama’s performance, with 72 per cent of respondents indicating that they approve of his administration’s performance. Meanwhile, 21 per cent of voters disapproved of the President’s performance, while 7 per cent had no opinion. The poll further assessed public perceptions of key government policies, with the Women’s Development Bank and the 24-Hour Economy receiving the lowest ratings among the initiatives evaluated. The Women’s Development Bank scored 4.6 out of 10, while the 24-Hour Economy received a rating of 4.2 out of 10. On the other hand, the No-Academic-Fee policy emerged as the highest-rated government initiative, scoring 6.1 out of 10. READ ALSO: 65% of Ghanaians back Mahama’s decision not to seek a third term — Global InfoAnalytics poll The “Big Push” infrastructure programme followed with a score of 6.0, while tax relief measures and the National Apprenticeship Programme recorded ratings of 5.8 and 5.5 respectively. The findings highlight varying levels of public confidence in the government’s overall direction and performance, while also reflecting mixed views on specific policy interventions.

items.title: Iran warns of ‘unforeseen’ consequences after Ukraine attack on Caspian Sea ship
items.description: Iran’s foreign ministry warned on Monday of “unforeseen” consequences following Ukraine’s attack on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea over the weekend. “This action by Ukraine was an absolutely illegal and unjustified act, contrary to the Charter of the United Nations, as well as a dangerous act of adventurism that will certainly not go unanswered by us,” the ministry’s spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said in a weekly press briefing. The consequences of Ukraine’s action “will certainly be unforeseen”, he added. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that Kyiv had carried out long-range strikes in the Caspian Sea against vessels transporting military cargo involving Iran. Iran said the attack had caused the Iranian ship “to explode, killing one sailor and injuring several others”, and warned that it would respond. “The Ukrainian regime must certainly be held accountable for it,” Baqaei said.
